German Stollen

Served at: First Sunday of Advent

Serves 12Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 15 min

German Stollen is a traditional fruit bread enjoyed during the Advent season, especially on the First Sunday of Advent. This rich, buttery bread is filled with dried fruits, nuts, and marzipan, symbolizing the festive spirit and anticipation of Christmas.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 packet (2 1/4 tsp) active dry yeast
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warm
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 tsp ground cardamom
  • 1 cup (150 g) mixed dried fruits (raisins, currants, chopped candied citrus peel)
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) chopped almonds or walnuts
  • 4 oz (115 g) marzipan roll (optional)
  • Powdered sugar for dusting
  • 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, melted (for brushing)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve yeast in warm milk and let sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt, cinnamon, and cardamom.
  3. Add the yeast mixture, softened butter, eggs, and vanilla extract to the dry ingredients and mix until a sticky dough forms.
  4. Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Fold in the dried fruits and chopped nuts evenly into the dough.
  6. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  7. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  8. Punch down the dough and roll it out into an oval shape about 1/2 inch (1.3 cm) thick.
  9. If using marzipan, roll it into a log about 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick and place it along the center of the dough.
  10. Fold the dough over the marzipan and shape it into a loaf, pinching the edges to seal.
  11. Place the loaf on a parchment-lined baking sheet and let it rise for another 30 minutes.
  12. Bake for 60-75 minutes until golden brown and cooked through; cover with foil if browning too quickly.
  13. Remove from oven and immediately brush the hot loaf with melted butter.
  14. Let cool slightly, then dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

Tips

  • For a moister Stollen, soak the dried fruits in rum or brandy overnight before adding to the dough.
  • Marzipan is traditional but optional; you can omit it for a simpler fruit bread.
  • Store Stollen wrapped tightly in foil or plastic wrap; it improves in flavor after a few days and can be frozen for longer storage.
